any index other than the clustered one. in InnoDB its entries hold the primary key, so a lookup descends twice

sqlite's default crash safety: copy the old pages aside, write new ones in place, delete the journal to commit
storing each column's values together instead of each row's, so a scan reads only the columns it names
operators pass batches of a few thousand values instead of one row per call
compressing a column as (value, count) pairs, which shrinks sorted or repetitive columns to almost nothing
replacing each value of a column with a small code into a list of its distinct values
